subject: Helios Health — competitive readiness & side-by-side probes
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ari Feldman <ari@helioshealth.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Helios Health — competitive readiness & side-by-side probes

Hi Ari / Sanjay,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to walk through where Helios is on the inference side and how you’re approaching the vendor run. I promised a concise recap of what we heard, the decision criteria we saw, open questions and a recommended side-by-side test plan you can use across vendors. I’m attaching a one-sheet and the test plan as an editable doc (see attachments).

Key pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent latency at peak (95th pctl spikes during end-of-day batch jobs)
- Cost unpredictability when traffic bursts and cloud egress spike
- Need for private deployment option for PHI-sensitive workflows (SOC2 + KMS)
- Long tail when model fallbacks happen (timeouts and retries)

Goals & decision criteria (preliminary):
1) End-to-end 95th pctl latency < 200ms for 1–2k TPS simulated workload
2) Predictable unit cost within 15% of baseline (current infra spend)
3) Private/VPN deployment with KMS integration and audit logs
4) Seamless model rollouts & automatic fallback with no client errors
5) Mature observability: token-level cost, per-request trace, model version SLOs

Open questions we need to close:
- Exact throughput envelope for the search / triage service (you mentioned 2k TPS as a target; can you confirm sustained vs burst?)
- Data residency constraints by customer cohort (US-only vs EU customers)
- Any procurement gating items beyond SOC2 (e.g., specific encryption certs / contractual clauses)

Proposed competitive side-by-side probes (summary):
- Latency / concurrency sweep (steady + burst patterns) with KV cache warm/cold phases
- Quantization parity: run 8-bit vs 16-bit and evaluate quality delta on your test prompts
- Failover/degeneration test: induce a model timeout to validate graceful fallback and client-level error rates
- Cost modeling: run a 48-hour synthetic load and compare billed token/throughput cost by vendor
- Security & compliance checklist: KMS integration, audit log retention, SOC2 artifacts produced

Attachments: helios-poc-requirements.xlsx (POC scope & dataset pointers), comparative-test-plan.md (editable test steps, metrics, pass/fail thresholds).

Next steps (what I’ll do / what we need from you):
- Marcus: push the editable test-plan to the shared Drive and seed the scripts for latency sweeps (by EOD Nov 4).
- Camila (technical): propose specific quantization settings to validate parity (will add to the test plan).
- Helios: share the representative request traces and confirm sustained vs burst TPS by Nov 5.
- Procurement: if you want, we can pull a short appendix of contractual clauses we typically see (I can draft that).

If that looks right, we can schedule the 1-hour run kickoff on Nov 9 to align infra owners and start the 48-hour run the next day.

Thanks again — happy to adjust these probes to match any additional constraints you have.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
attachments: helios-poc-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), comparative-test-plan.md (markdown)

Subject: Re: Helios Health — competitive readiness & side-by-side probes

Thanks Marcus — this is a great recap and aligns with what the team heard. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Throughput: confirmed target is 2k TPS sustained for core triage flow, with 5k TPS short bursts (under 5 minutes) during peak windows.
- Data residency: primary requirement is US region for PHI; later phases will include EU customers (we'll flag those with a tag).
- Procurement: SOC2 + ISO 27001 are required; for now we do not need extra encryption certs beyond KMS/HSM capability, but procurement will confirm.

We’ll upload a sanitized request trace by EOD Nov 5. Also — can you include a short paragraph in the test-plan that explains how to measure perceived quality differences for quantized models? Our clinical team will want to see an evaluation rubric not just token-loss.

Ari
Ari Feldman
VP, Emerging Tech
Helios Health

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 9:21 AM Ari Feldman <ari@helioshealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — this is a great recap and aligns with what the team heard. Quick clarifications from our side:
> 
> - Throughput: confirmed target is 2k TPS sustained for core triage flow, with 5k TPS short bursts (under 5 minutes) during peak windows.
> - Data residency: primary requirement is US region for PHI; later phases will include EU customers (we'll flag those with a tag).
> - Procurement: SOC2 + ISO 27001 are required; for now we do not need extra encryption certs beyond KMS/HSM capability, but procurement will confirm.

Thanks for the clarifications Ari — that helps. I’ve updated the comparative-test-plan.md with explicit test cases and pass criteria. Summary of what I added: 

- Quantization quality rubric: clinical prompt set (n=120), accept per-prompt delta tolerance: 95% of prompts must maintain clinical-actionable parity (evaluated by redacted clinician labels). Guidance includes example scoring (0-3 severity) and automated BLEU/F1 + manual spot checks.
- Latency sweep details: steady-state 2k TPS (95th pctl target < 200ms), burst injection to 5k TPS for 3x 3-minute windows, and cold vs warm KV cache comparisons.
- Failover behaviour: simulate model eviction to validate automatic fallback to a smaller variant and measure client retries and error surface.
- Security checks: confirm KMS encryption at rest, HSM-backed key option, and whether audit logs include token-level trace for seven days (we noted you asked for longer retention — please confirm exact window).

I attached short run scripts and a checklist in the Drive. I also noted a small vendor-specific ask: we’ll need an SSH-based access window for the run-engine team to collect low-level perf counters (we can do read-only ops). Let me know if that’s OK.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: comparative-test-plan.md (updated), run-scripts.tar.gz (stub)
